newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end down on weak demand for new 4-year notes.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end down on weak demand for new 4-year notes.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly lower on Tuesday.
Speculation that investors' appetite for the newly auctioned four-year notes might be weaker than expected weighed down the March in the early afternoon, traders said.
The Ministry of Finance offered 500 billion yen worth of 1.1 percent four-year notes through a price-competitive auction on Tuesday.
Earlier, there were some expectations that the four-year notes would be offered with a coupon rate of 1.2 percent.
"When the (four-year) notes were offered at 1.1 percent, it led to speculation that buying needs among regional investors might weaken," a trust bank trader said.
A trader for a trust bank's securities affiliate said, however, that there seemed to be moderate demand for the new four-year issues.
The March ended at 126.22 on Tuesday, down from the previous day's 126.35.
Turnover was 44,241 contracts.
Some said the market was dragged down in the afternoon by large-lot selling of the March.
Large-lot sales of the March JGB futures totalling about 50 billion yen at around 126.20 dampened the mood of the market, a trader at a city bank's securities unit said.
The selling seemed to have come from a foreign financial institution and was probably an attempt to drive down the market, the trust bank trader said.
"What happens is they first place bids and afterwards put in large-lot sell orders," the trader said.
When bids seemingly disappear as a result of such trading, it can have a negative psychological impact on the market, the trader said.
Some traders said a lecture by the Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita may also have had some negative impact.
The BOJ governor told a business symposium on Tuesday that the strength of Japan's private sector demand was becoming recognisable.
Matsushita said private-sector demand was strengthening despite the fact that public spending was declining, showing that a favourable economic cycle was moving forward.
He also said that the BOJ would continue to conduct its monetary policy with the aim of ensuring a basis for a self-sustainable economic recovery.
Others in the market said, however, that the governor's comments had little impact on the JGB market.
"Market participants are taking a more long-term view of the economy. They are not focusing so much on the current state of the economy," the trust bank trader said.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.390 percent as of 0725 GMT, up from previous day's 2.380 percent.
Nippon Credit Bank's January five-year bank debenture was traded at a yield of 4.10 percent on Tuesday. The Industrial Bank of Japan's January five-year bank debenture was traded at 1.62 percent.
